title: The Woman of Strength
lead: The 'eshet chayil, "woman of strength", is the subject of the alphabet poem that closes Proverbs (31:10–31), named also in Proverbs 12:4 and given as Boaz's description of Ruth (Ruth 3:11). Jews sing the poem on Friday evenings, and Christians have read her as the church, as Mary, as Wisdom and as a model for women's lives.

sections.b: The phrase 'eshet chayil occurs three times. Proverbs 12:4 makes her "her husband's crown". Proverbs 31:10 asks, "who can find one?", and the poem that follows praises her work, trade, care for the poor and fear of the LORD. In Ruth, Boaz says, "the whole town knows that you are a woman of worth" (Ruth 3:11; this site renders the same Hebrew as "a woman of worth" there, and as "a woman of strength" in Proverbs). In the Hebrew Bible, Ruth follows Proverbs directly in the Leningrad Codex and in editions based on it, such as Biblia Hebraica Stuttgartensia, so the reader moves from the poem to a real woman of strength, a Moabite widow. Boaz himself is a gibbor chayil, "a man of great worth" (Ruth 2:1).
